title: Ideal-quotient comparison for an adequately affine stack
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $P$ a commutative $k$-algebra, and $f:\mathcal Z\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ an adequately affine morphism [def-sfb-adequately-affine-morphism, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\mathcal A$ be any quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}$-algebra [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], put $G=\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal A)$, and let $I\subseteq P$ be any ideal. Write $I\mathcal A$ for the quasi-coherent ideal generated by the image of $I$, and $IG$ for the ideal generated by its image in $G$. Quotients are the rings or algebra sheaves imposing these ideal relations. The canonical map
$$v:G/IG\longrightarrow H=\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal A/I\mathcal A)$$
has the following property: for every commutative $G/IG$-algebra $E$, the homomorphism $v_E:E\to E\otimes_{G/IG}H$, $e\mapsto e\otimes1$, has elementwise nilpotent kernel, and every element $h$ of its target has a positive power $h^N$ in its image. Tensor extension uses [def-weil-module-base-change]. There is no condition that $P\to G$ be an isomorphism, and no finite-generation, flatness, Noetherian or absolute diagonal-separation hypothesis.

source.place: Alper Lemma 5.2.1, printed p.507, with Proposition 3.3.5 and Remark 3.3.2, printed pp.497--498: algebraic consequence of the ideal-quotient adequate homeomorphism after every scalar extension. Published primary PDF: https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf (read online; local PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal J=I\mathcal A$, $K=\Gamma(\mathcal Z,\mathcal J)$, $R=G/IG$ and $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\mathcal J^mT^m$. The polynomial/Rees calculus makes $\mathcal J$, $\mathcal A/\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal R$ quasi-coherent and gives $K\subseteq G$ (degree one of $\Gamma(\mathcal R)\subseteq G[T]$), so $K$ is an ideal; on each smooth affine chart $V$ it gives $\mathcal J_V=I\mathcal A_V$, hence $(\mathcal A/\mathcal J)_V=\mathcal A_V/I\mathcal A_V$ and $\mathcal R_V\subseteq\mathcal A_V[T]$. Apply smooth-cover section descent to a small family of all smooth affine charts $V_i\to\mathcal Z$, and to each relation space $R_{ij}$ with its etale affine charts (again smooth affine charts of $\mathcal Z$). If $b\in K$, each $b|_{V_i}\in I\mathcal A_{V_i}$ maps to $0$, so $b\mapsto0$ in $H$. If $b\mapsto0$ in $H$, each $b|_{V_i}\in I\mathcal A_{V_i}$, so $b|_{V_i}T\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal R)$; these agree on every $R_{ij}$, as they do in $\mathcal A[T]$ and $\Gamma(R_{ij},\mathcal R)\to\Gamma(R_{ij},\mathcal A[T])$ is injective on charts, and descend to $bT\in\Gamma(\mathcal R)$, i.e. $b\in K$. Hence $K=\ker(G\to H)$. Every structural element of $I$ lies in $K$, so $IG\subseteq K$, $v:R\to H$ is defined, and $\ker v=K/IG$.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.1, first factorization; kernel identification from compatible families Published primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Choose generators $(a_j)_{j\in J}$ of $I$ (all elements of $I$ suffice). The cited calculus gives the unital graded surjection $q:\mathcal A[x_j]\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus_{m\geq0}\mathcal J^mT^m$, $x_j\mapsto a_jT$, and identifies its source sections with $G[x_j]$ and its target with a graded subring of $G[T]$. Since $f$ is adequately affine over the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}P$, the affine-target criterion applies to this very surjection. For $b\in K$, apply it to the global homogeneous section $bT$ to obtain $N>0$ and a finite polynomial $Q=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$ with $\Gamma(q)(Q)=(bT)^N$. Equality of the degree-$N$ coefficients gives $b^N=\sum_{|\alpha|=N}c_\alpha a^\alpha\in IG$: each monomial in this finite sum has at least one factor $a_j$ because $N>0$. Therefore every element of $K/IG=\ker v$ is nilpotent. Neither an exponent uniform in $b$ nor finite generation of $I$ is used.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.1, graded power-lifting argument Published primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For every finite $n\geq0$, apply the polynomial/Rees calculus to the surjection $\mathcal A\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal A/\mathcal J$. It gives a surjection $\mathcal A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow(\mathcal A/\mathcal J)[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ of quasi-coherent algebras and identifies the corresponding section map with $G[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to H[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. The affine-target criterion says that every polynomial in $H[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ has a positive power in its image. This map factors coefficientwise through $R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, since $IG$ maps to zero in $H$. Passing the lifting polynomial to this quotient shows that every polynomial extension $v_n:R[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\to H[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ lifts positive powers.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.8, polynomial-extension argument, applied to the quotient in Lemma 5.2.1 Published primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The preceding two steps establish precisely the hypotheses of the ring polynomial-test lemma for $v:R\to H$: its kernel is elementwise nilpotent and each finite polynomial extension lifts positive powers. Apply that lemma to any commutative $R$-algebra $E$. It gives an elementwise nilpotent kernel for $E\to E\otimes_RH$ and, for each element of the latter ring, a positive power in the image. Its unit map is $e\mapsto e\otimes1$, which is the map $v_E$ of the statement. This proves both clauses with the prescribed arbitrary scalar extension.

source.place: Remark 3.2.2 and the spectral part of Proposition 3.3.5 Published primary PDF https://content.algebraicgeometry.nl/2014-4/2014-4-022.pdf read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof_origin.place: Expansion of Alper Lemma 5.2.1 and the polynomial argument in Lemma 4.1.8, with Remark 3.2.2; published PDF read online, local copy WANTED.
